Marathon Petroleum rose 0.86% today as crude oil prices stabilized and refining conditions remained supportive. U.S. crude held steady around $96 per barrel while domestic refineries ran at a healthy 92.5% utilization rate, providing a steady backdrop for refining margins. The stock has been volatile over the past two weeks (down 4.47%), but today's bounce follows yesterday's gains as oil prices found some footing.

The broader energy picture offers mixed signals for refiners. Talk of a potential diesel export ban from the Trump administration could tighten U.S. fuel supplies and potentially lift margins on refined products sold domestically, which would be positive for refiners—though the industry has warned such a ban could raise prices. At the same time, geopolitical uncertainty around Iran sanctions and the Strait of Hormuz remains a wild card for crude supply flows.
